A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, algorithms and principal theoretical results. Text extraction and visual inspection cover all pages, including figures, tables and appendices; relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original Rastrigin simulations, empirical probability curves and optimization outcomes in Tables 1–2. The simulated-annealing baseline values are separately attributed to prior work.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original simulations and reports additional Langevin-method comparisons and dimensionality experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, their update formulas and the annealing schedule remain unchanged. Algorithm 2 now explicitly conditions sampling on the current iterate, clarifying dependence already established by its formulas and v1 Appendix A.2.

E1.justification: v2 Figure 4 adds optimization experiments on 20-dimensional Rastrigin, extending v1's tested 10-dimensional search space. Coverage remains confined to the same synthetic function; the one- and two-dimensional illustrations are retained material.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 2 adds evaluated comparisons against the overdamped Langevin algorithm (OLA, Vempala and Wibisono, 2019) and underdamped Langevin algorithm (ULA, Ma et al., 2021). These were discussed but not experimentally compared in v1. Table 2 retains SA, FSA, SMC-SA and CSA.

E3.justification: The new sampler comparison uses common, empirically selected (a, epsilon) pairs of (4, 2) and (3, 4). The dimensionality analysis compares d=10, epsilon=2 with d=20, epsilon=4, and the annealing evaluation adds epsilon=0.25. Previously stated experimental budgets and settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds dimensionality sensitivity analysis in Figure 4 and extends the annealing sensitivity analysis to a stricter accuracy threshold in Figure 5. The existing temperature studies and fixed-effort sample-versus-iteration analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report M=100 runs for the basic probability experiment and M=50 with averages and standard deviations for Table 2. No new seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: New Figures 2 and 4 add sampler-comparison and d=20 results; HRLA and OLA reach high success probabilities earlier than ULA in the displayed settings. Figure 5 adds epsilon=0.25 and revises existing annealing curves: for final a=40 and epsilon=0.5, the displayed plateau changes from approximately 0.80 in v1 Figure 4 to 0.73. Tables 1–2 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Remark 2.3 changes the justification for transferring the log-Sobolev property to the product Gibbs measure from convolution to tensorization, also added to Remark 2.1. The principal assumptions, convergence bounds and appendix proof calculations are otherwise unchanged; v1 Assumption 3.1 becomes v2 Assumption B.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusions retain the same claims: high-probability global optimization using an oracle sampler and a proposed high-resolution Langevin sampler. The added aspiration for future acceleration breakthroughs does not establish a new claimed result.

C2.justification: New Remark 4.7 explicitly acknowledges that the proved rates do not improve on existing Langevin bounds and attributes this to limitations of the analysis. Section 5 also adds an interpretation of dimensionality scaling through proportional tolerance adjustment. Existing parameter-selection and cooling-schedule limitations remain.

D1.justification: The added sampler comparison documents empirical selection of a for each accuracy threshold and supplies the shared parameter pairs in Figure 2. Python 3.8, the Cronos HPC disclosure, code access and the existing HRLA parameter recipe remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shi et al. (2022), Su et al. (2016), Bakry et al. (2014), and Chewi and Stromme (2024), expanding discussion of high-resolution dynamics and log-Sobolev inequalities. It also positions the latter assumption as uncommon in global optimization. Publication updates to existing references are not new cited works.

P1.justification: The introduction and motivation receive limited expansions, several passages are tightened, and Algorithm 2's conditional-sampling wording is clarified. Technical assumptions move into Appendix B, with deferred proofs relabeled Appendix C; the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from one column to two columns, substantially changing layout. Existing probability plots are rearranged into different panel grids, the annealing display expands from three panels to four, and two comparison figures are added. The Rastrigin illustration moves to Appendix A, and tables are restyled and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies direct comparisons with closely related Langevin samplers, adds dimensionality and stricter-tolerance checks, and more clearly acknowledges the absence of improved theoretical rates. These strengthen empirical context and clarify limitations. The gains remain limited to one synthetic benchmark, while the algorithms, principal guarantees and appendix proofs are essentially unchanged.
